title: Extract all refinement fields when refining ambiguous input into a wagon

facts.note: Decisive fact: the planner holds AMBIGUOUS input (unclear subject, intent, scope, ownership or success) that must be refined into a structured wagon. Free-form or unstructured format is only one possible form of ambiguous input; format alone does not qualify — clear input, however formatted, does not activate the rule. Presence or absence of acceptance criteria does not decide ambiguity. Bare terms like 'wagon' are not sufficient.
Candidate signal only: a wagon definition file is being written. Does not by itself establish refinement of ambiguous input.
Candidate signal only: a diff observer could detect a new wagon definition; linking it to ambiguous source input still needs judgement.

fires: Planner turns an ambiguous feature request or idea (unclear who acts, why, or what counts as done) into a new structured wagon definition
Planner is asked to refine a vague wagon draft whose intent, scope or artifact ownership is ambiguous into its structured fields
doesNotFire: Input is already clear and unambiguous, even if written as free-form prose
Planner edits a single field (e.g. theme only) of an already-refined wagon without refining new ambiguous input
Coder implements code inside an already-refined wagon
Documentation-only edits that do not refine input into a wagon

given: A planner holds ambiguous input (possibly free-form) that must become a structured wagon.
when: Refining that input into a wagon definition.
then: Extract subject, action, goal, context, outcome, produce, consume and theme into the wagon definition.
prefer: subject: WHO/WHAT performs the action (actor:role or entity:state).
produce: owned output artifacts; consume: input artifacts owned by other wagons.

theme: one of mechanic, scenario, match, sensory, player, league, audience, monetization, partnership, commons — pick the one whose scope matches (scopes in shared:context.planner.wagon-theme-taxonomy).
avoid: Non-present-tense actions; goals with several intents; unmeasurable outcomes.
Other wagons' artifacts under produce, or own artifacts under consume.
Themes outside the taxonomy; descriptions under 10 characters.
why: Structured fields make the wagon's intent, scope, ownership and success checkable; later coherence checks validate exactly these fields.
evidence: Wagon definition contains subject, action, goal, context, outcome, produce, consume and theme fields.
subject matches actor:role or entity:state; context is comma-separated conditions; theme is a member of the canonical theme taxonomy.
Every produce artifact is owned by this wagon; every consume artifact is owned by another wagon.
verifier_detail: Field map (field -> what to extract): subject = WHO/WHAT performs the action (actor:role or entity:state); action = core present-tense verb phrase; goal = WHY/motivation, single intent statement; context = WHEN/WHERE, comma-separated conditions; outcome = measurable progress statement (measurable result); produce = owned output artifacts; consume = input artifacts owned by other wagons.

theme -> scope: validate theme against the taxonomy in shared:context.planner.wagon-theme-taxonomy (allowed values: mechanic, scenario, match, sensory, player, league, audience, monetization, partnership, commons).
Terms ids: extraction_field ('Refinement fields'), wagon_theme ('Wagon theme options').
audit: parity: source_fragments_preserved=true, examples_preserved=false, implementation_preserved=false, fix_hint_preserved=false, reviewed_at=2026-06-16
Original statement: 'Refine ambiguous input into a structured wagon by extracting subject, action, goal, context, outcome, produce/consume artifacts, and theme.'

sharedNodes.text: Wagon theme options (theme -> scope): mechanic = Core game rules, decision systems, and immediate feedback loops; scenario = Content ingestion, entity extraction, and narrative structure processing; match = Session orchestration, state management, and lifecycle control, Multi-player coordination, turn management; sensory = UI rendering, audio mixing, gesture capture, and player interaction; player = Individual lifecycle, onboarding, progression, and session management; league = Competitive organization, bracket management, and tournament operations; audience = Spectator engagement, streaming infrastructure, and viewer participation; monetization = Token economy, wallet operations, and transaction processing; partnership = Sponsor/partner onboarding, delegation, and commercial integration; commons = Shared infrastructure, cross-cutting utilities, and platform services.

additions.text: Avoid items are direct negations of the source field definitions: unextracted field, non-present-tense action, multi-intent goal, unmeasurable outcome, misplaced produce/consume, off-taxonomy theme, description < 10 chars.
additions.justification: Source states only positive definitions; these negations add no new obligation.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires and doesNotFire situations, scoped strictly to refining ambiguous input into a wagon; free-form format is only a possible form of ambiguous input, never a qualifying condition on its own.
additions.justification: Required by target schema; derived from the source statement ('Refine ambiguous input'). file_kind/change are marked as candidate signals only.
Source has no rationale; derived from the statement and graph edge 'extraction produces the fields coherence checks validate'.

additions.text: Theme value names listed inline in prefer[6] with a pointer to the shared taxonomy node for scopes.
additions.justification: Lets the planner choose a theme without external lookup of allowed values; names come verbatim from the source term keys. Coder-facing text may slightly exceed ~1,000 chars to keep this lossless and usable.

additions.text: No separate convention proposed; the description-length minimum is supporting guidance (prefer[7]/avoid[3]/evidence[1]) of the same wagon-definition decision, not part of the single 'then' obligation.
additions.justification: Keeps 'then' to one extraction obligation as required by the auditor.

additions.text: Theme taxonomy moved to new node context.planner.wagon-theme-taxonomy (needs dedup review; overlaps planner.theme.canonical-taxonomy).
additions.justification: Taxonomy is domain-specific and shared with planner.theme.canonical-taxonomy (graph 'requires' edge); keeps coder-facing text codebase-neutral while preserving it losslessly.
